name: ogmtools
why: Manipulating OGG media stream internals exposes container structure, an obscure old format worth a poke but a thin hook.

brief.what_it_is: OGMtools is a set of Linux command-line tools for OGG media streams, which the author abbreviates as OGM. The homepage lists five executables: ogmcat, ogmdemux, ogminfo, ogmmerge and ogmsplit. Per the homepage, ogminfo reports information about an OGM file, ogmdemux extracts streams from one, and ogmmerge creates one. The homepage names no inputs or outputs beyond these, and it does not describe ogmcat or ogmsplit.
brief.why_it_exists: The author says OggMux was the source of the idea, but OggMux is Windows-only, so these tools bring that kind of OGM handling to Linux. The homepage is titled "OGMtools for Linux".
brief.install_notes: The homepage offers only a source tarball, ogmtools-1.5.tar.bz2 (209kb). It gives no build steps, dependencies, or configuration. The brew formula is the easier route, but the homepage itself says nothing about build requirements.
brief.standout: It is a small, focused, Linux-side counterpart to a Windows tool (OggMux) that the author credits, and it pairs with a separate Windows toolset by Cyrius that the author also praises. Its niche is inspecting and rewriting the internal stream structure of Ogg files.
brief.status: abandoned. The homepage shows no release or update date. The brew caveat says the project has not been updated since 2004 and is no longer being developed, maintained or supported.
brief.caveats: The brew caveat says there are several issues, especially on 64-bit architectures, and the author will not fix them or accept patches. The homepage gives no command examples, and its documentation links (README, ChangeLog, man pages for each tool) were not followed, so usage details are unverified. The tools are Linux-focused, and the homepage gives no license.
quotes: These tools allow information about (ogminfo) or extraction from (ogmdemux) or creation of (ogmmerge) OGG media streams.
Note that I'll use OGM for "OGG media streams".
OggMux is the utility that I got my ideas from - but it's for Windows only.
fetch_log: https://www.bunkus.org/videotools/ogmtools/ - worked; returned the homepage text with the description, source tarball name and size, and a list of documentation pages (README, ChangeLog, man pages for ogmmerge, ogminfo, ogmdemux, ogmsplit, ogmcat, dvdxchap). The page text did not include their URLs, so I did not follow them.
